headline: Treasury gets permanent access to Social Security death records to stop federal payments to dead people, with new safeguards against false death listings.
what_it_does: The law makes permanent a requirement that the Social Security Administration (SSA) share its full death records with Treasury's Do Not Pay system, which checks federal payments before they go out. That sharing had been set to last only three years. Treasury must reach an agreement with SSA on its share of the cost of state death data. SSA may not list someone as dead unless it has clear and convincing evidence, and it may alert other agencies if a living person was wrongly listed and sends proof.

who_it_affects.group: People wrongly listed as dead by Social Security
who_it_affects.how: If they send supporting documents, SSA may notify Treasury and federal or state benefit agencies so their records can be corrected.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive federal or federally funded benefits
who_it_affects.how: Their payments can be checked against Social Security death records, with a higher evidence standard required before SSA marks anyone as dead.

who_it_affects.group: Families of people who have died
who_it_affects.how: Federal payments still going to a deceased relative are more likely to be stopped or recovered.

who_it_affects.group: Federal and state agencies that pay out federal funds
who_it_affects.how: They can rely on permanent access to SSA death data through Treasury's Do Not Pay system to prevent and recover improper payments.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 10, 2026; the summary does not give separate start dates for specific provisions.
